svg.title: The live feed's new signals against the controls
svg.desc: False new signals per 100 targets: what the feed's own admission rule passes on light curves with every signal destroyed, against the live feed. Wilson 95% intervals; a target is 2 sectors. Live feed under the old rule, “new” signals: 15.8 per 100 targets (3 over 19 targets; 5.5–37.6); Control: block-scrambled light curves: 12.3 per 100 targets (19 over 309 star-sectors; 7.9–18.8); Control: flux-inverted light curves: 11.7 per 100 targets (18 over 309 star-sectors; 7.4–18.0); Real light curves of TOI hosts: 4.5 per 100 targets (7 over 309 star-sectors; 2.2–9.2); Feed-rule test, old rule: worse control: 27.8 per 100 targets (86 over 309 targets; 23.1–33.1); Feed-rule test, two-sector rule: worse control: 6.1 per 100 targets (19 over 309 targets; 4.0–9.4); Live feed re-run, two-sector rule: 0.0 per 100 targets (0 over 19 targets; 0.0–16.8). Expected from noise alone (the worse control): 12.3 per 100 targets, so the live feed's “new” signals were consistent with noise under the old rule. The pre-registered two-sector rule (FAP < 0.001 over 2,000 trials, the signal in both sectors), measured on the held-out half with the discovery config on the current code, lowers the worse control 4.5-fold, but noise still outnumbers the 1.6 real new signals per 100 targets, so admissions are leads for review. Source: docs/results/benchmark_real_tois_clipfix.json (held-out half, feed-level table, feed_rule), commit d6f8ae8.
